boundaries.label: Reader's browser · owned source and attempts

cards.title: One source owner; several responsibilities
items: The public entry composes the UI/session, parser, preparation, geometry and lookup factories. Selection, edits, cancel, clear and replacement revoke stale commits. Arrows summarize owned data/operation relationships, not direct worker-to-worker channels.

Parser records return through PDF.js's main-thread proxy. The session forwards source-linked chunks, vectors and candidates. Context assembly preserves the exact accepted question and complete selected evidence before a separate explicit Generate action.

cards.title: Two outcomes remain independent
items: A completed Qwen attempt produces a complete raw receipt. EOS, JSON shape and selected citation identity decide whether the UI shows an unverified draft or a refusal; those gates do not adjudicate financial truth.

The six-field comparator binds a supported Net income cell to frozen native parser records. Unsupported or ambiguous requests refuse. It neither parses natural-language intent nor changes Qwen output; currency normalization stays unset.

cards.title: Prepared bytes are not executable readiness
items: Explicit preparation uses a separate worker without a PDF, question or model invocation. Site is the default; explicit HF prepares only five immutable model files. The three inference runtime files and SDK imports remain on site, with unchanged logical cache keys and pins.

Native attempts verify inside their own workers/runtime loaders and read shared cache bodies; they do not invoke the optional preparation worker. Owned WASM reuse retains an additional 21,596,019-byte ArrayBuffer; it is not zero-copy. Public PDF selection separately verifies its script within 120 seconds before unchanged 10-second native readiness. Ordinary HTTP cache reuse is advisory.

cards.title: Current source architecture; separate acceptance gates
items: This October 11, 2026 implementation overview is pinned to source commit 7c7a2c39375c29bdef3675d88a4e9a8aa8b610a7. It shows browser responsibilities; runtime observations, financial-quality evaluation and human verdicts have separate evidence.
The separately packaged AGPL Python API is not called by this browser and is not hosted by GitHub Pages. Its injected service and package/HTTP acceptance have their own scope.

The editable specification, rendered figure and committed-source references are checked together. Those artifact checks describe this architecture; native execution and financial acceptance remain separate gates.
